name: Manchu sky
summary: Shamanic constellations of the hunting and fishing people of northeast China: the Seven Maidens, the Divine Eagle, the shaman’s drum and drumstick.

Narhu.name: The Seven Maidens
Narhu.description: The Pleiades. In Manchu myth they are helpers of the star-scattering goddess and the leaders of the stars: rising in the east at dusk, they lead the procession of winter stars towards the west. An important sign of the beginning of winter and of night-time keeping.

Sengge.name: The God of Hedgehogs
Sengge.description: The constellation Cygnus in the middle of the Milky Way. It was also called the “Rafter Star” or the “Hedgehog Star”; a deity who guards the night and the home, and an important northern guide star.

Taci.name: Grandmother Taci
Taci.description: The W shape of Cassiopeia. The celestial goddess entrusted her with measuring time for the gods day and night: the hour was estimated from her position and tilt in the sky.

Tobo.name: The Hut
Tobo.description: The stars of Perseus: a hut where the shaman’s soul rests while ascending to the sky.

Tehe.name: The God of the Stand
Tehe.description: The great square of Pegasus and its surroundings. Shamans watched it for signs of wind and snowfall.

Ilan.name: The Three Stars
Ilan.description: The three stars of Orion’s Belt. When they rise in the east at dusk, it is midwinter; from their course the hours of the second half of the night were estimated. The counterpart of the Hungarian Reapers’ Star.

Nadan.name: The Seven Stars
Nadan.description: The Plough, the most important star group for night-time keeping and for the northern direction. “When its handle points north, winter rules the earth.”

Gasha.name: The Divine Eagle
Gasha.description: A huge eagle spreading its wings across the stars of Orion, Taurus, Auriga and Gemini. It dominates the midwinter sky; weather was predicted from its shape. Its right foot is led by the Seven Maidens, its left is tied by a celestial rope (Eridanus).

Singgeri.name: The Rat
Singgeri.description: The stars of Leo: the rat goddess who greets the dawn, rising in the east before the winter dawn to receive the rays of the Sun.

Morin.name: The Horse
Morin.description: Not really a constellation but a seasonal collective name for four bright stars (Capella, Sirius, Arcturus, Spica); here Sirius stands for it.

Wadan.name: The Celestial Altar
Wadan.description: The constellation Corvus: the heavenly place where ritual objects are kept. When someone was learning to be a shaman, or a shaman died, this star had to be honoured.

Imcin.name: The Drum
Imcin.description: In the region of Aries, Triangulum and Andromeda: the shaman’s drum of the star-scattering goddess.

Gisun.name: The Drumstick
Gisun.description: The faint row of stars next to the Drum: the stick that beats the shaman’s drum.

Siri.name: Goddess of the Carp
Siri.description: The faint stars of Lynx and Camelopardalis. According to the legend she turned into a carp to track down a demon that had fled into the river; the mistress of the fish of the icy rivers, from which the luck of winter fishing was foretold.

Terkin.name: Goddess of the Stairs
Terkin.description: The stars of Virgo and Coma Berenices: a “stairway to the sky”, a seated goddess who helps the shaman’s soul to ascend.

Buruhun.name: The Dawn Beast
Buruhun.description: Boötes and its neighbours: the three-eared, six-eyed beast of dawn, sent by the celestial goddess to lead the Sun’s rays before the winter dawn.

Fodoho.name: The Willow
Fodoho.description: The head of Hydra, low in the southern sky: the divine star of the blessing of children; the harvest and epidemics were also foretold from it.

Asu.name: The Net
Asu.description: The stars of Hercules: the net of the god of hunting, a mirror of the fishing and hunting way of life.

Nimaha.name: The Hook
Nimaha.description: The constellation Scorpius: a fish hook. A summer deity called the “warm star”; from its appearance the time of farming and the harvest were foretold.

Hadaha.name: The Nail
Hadaha.description: The Pole Star, around which the sky turns.

Juru.name: The Two Silver-Maned Steeds
Juru.description: The two brighter stars of the Little Bear, Kochab and Pherkad.

Ikiri.name: The Ox-Leading Stars
Ikiri.description: The bright Altair and its two neighbours in the constellation Aquila.

Ilmahu.name: The Supporting Pole
Ilmahu.description: The stars of Orion’s Sword, below the Three Stars.

Borboho.name: The Coiled Strap
Borboho.description: The semicircle of Corona Borealis: a coiled leather strap.
